subject.title: [Feature]: Add before_persistence_write hook for durable state changes

question: Should OpenClaw add a dedicated `before_persistence_write` Plugin SDK hook for durable state writes, or should this capability be modeled through existing tool/policy/provenance hooks?
rationale: This is a public Plugin SDK enforcement boundary over persisted user and agent state, so automation cannot safely choose the taxonomy, payload exposure, block/mutate semantics, or failure policy without maintainer security and product intent.

options.title: Design a dedicated hook
options.body: Add a narrowly scoped `before_persistence_write` contract with redacted payloads, explicit write-target taxonomy, bounded execution, and tests for representative memory/file/cron/config writers.

options.title: Extend existing tool hooks
options.body: Keep a single tool-policy surface by enriching `before_tool_call` with durable-write metadata, accepting that non-tool persistence writes may still need separate coverage.

options.title: Defer into provenance work
options.body: Keep this thread open but require the broader persistent-state provenance design to decide write and read semantics together before implementation.

recommendation.title: Design a dedicated hook
recommendation.body: Add a narrowly scoped `before_persistence_write` contract with redacted payloads, explicit write-target taxonomy, bounded execution, and tests for representative memory/file/cron/config writers.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the clearest maintainer-routing signal from the generic host-hook foundation history and are better positioned than feature contributors to decide a public Plugin SDK/security boundary.
